body:
**Findings-triage round — PROMOTED to `pm:queue`, but scoped as a CLASS fix, ⛔ not as a fourth instance.**

## Why it is promoted

Concrete, located, and it restores an invariant rather than proposing a capability. Premise re-checked on `origin/main` at grading time: `nameField` is still referenced at the read exits in `protocol.ts`, and `provisionSearchCompanion*` — the half #8038 already built — is live in both `protocol.ts` and `objectql/src/core.ts`. So the seam and the precedent both still exist.

## ⛔ The scope ruling, which is the point of this promotion

**Three materialization stamps have now diverged on ONE seam, one at a time:** #6562 (system columns, ruled Option B) → #8038 (`__search`, built `provisionSearchCompanionOnto`) → this card (`nameField`). Fixing `nameField` alone makes it four next time.

⇒ The deliverable is *"materialize this base the way the registry materializes its own"* **at the read exits**, reusing the mechanism #8038 built rather than adding a third stamp-specific patch. Whoever takes this must **enumerate the stamps that cross that seam** and say which are covered and which are not — an inventory in the PR body, in the shape #8334 used for its producer sweep. A partial fix with a stated inventory is acceptable; an unstated one is not.

## ⚠️ What this is NOT entangled with — settled here so it is not re-litigated

The seat post warned to read this together with **#8284** and **#8037** because `nameField`, `label`, `pluralLabel` and `description` are all scalars resolved last-writer-wins. Read them, but note the mechanisms are **different** and this card is not blocked on that decision:

- **#8284 / #8037** are **i18n precedence** — `translateObject` resolves `catalog ?? document` and the catalog wins unconditionally. That fork is in the maintainer's inbox.
- **This card** is a **materialization stamp** at the read exit, the same seam as #6562 and #8038.

⇒ Dispatchable now. ⛔ Do not wait on #8284, and ⛔ do not let a fix here quietly change i18n precedence — if the work reaches `translateObject`, stop and report the collision.

Grading happens here rather than at filing time, per the lane's rule: the dev that filed it had local visibility only and correctly did not level it.

## Landed — `75fd301d` on `main`. Closing, with the remainder named.

Confirmed by both readings: the merge event and the commit on `origin/main` (11:08:44Z), never the `auto_merge` field. PR #8380. The trailer was `Part of`, so this closure is deliberate rather than automatic — the reasoning is below.

### Delivered

The card's named defect, both halves: `GET /meta/object/:name` no longer drops `nameField` for artifact-ingested objects, and the write-side inverse strips it back off so the served stamp cannot bake into a tenant's stored row.

More importantly, the thing this card was *promoted* for. It was the third ruling on one seam (#6562 → #8038 → #8268), so it was dispatched as a **class fix**, and that is what shipped: `registerObject`'s materialization block is now a single method, `materializeServedObjectOnto` replays it onto a body that never came through `registerObject`, and the read exits ask for the whole seam via `materializeFromRegistry` instead of naming a stamp. A stamp added to that block converges on served documents the day it is added — no fourth method, and no fourth card for the same reason.

### ⛔ This closure is NOT a claim the seam is now uniform

Three defects on this seam remain, each separately owned:

| card | what is left | state |
|---|---|---|
| **#8375** | the multi-tenant `indexes` stamp has no converger at all — the read exit converges the fields map only | `pm:queue`, this lane |
| **#8376** | the read exits materialize the *folded* object while the registry materializes the *base* | ⛔ `needs-user-decision` — one branch is schema-migration-bearing, so it is the maintainer's |
| **#8381** | the `nameField` strip drops an author's redundant pointer — and ⚠️ [option C as filed is equivalent to option A](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/8381#issuecomment-5279591027) on the case it exists to fix; read that before starting | `pm:queue`, this lane |

**Why close rather than leave open.** None of the three declares `Blocked-by: #8268`, so closing creates no circular block — and leaving it open would park a card in the pool whose content is now fully duplicated across three children, which is the shape #7654 and #8136 were closed to avoid earlier in this shift.

### The generalizable finding, worth more than the patch

From the PR's own stamp inventory: **the stamp that _delegates_ to the registry (`__search`) has not drifted; the stamp with _no converger_ (`nameField`) was simply missing; the stamp converged by a _second implementation_ of its producer (`applyInjectedSystemColumns` vs `applySystemFields`) is the one that silently disagrees.** That is exactly the shape `d5031f6a1` fixed next door by deleting a second implementation and calling the canonical one — and it is still live here, which is what #8375 is.

Two process notes also worth keeping: known-but-unfixed divergences were pinned as *deliberate tripwires* rather than left silent, so the day either is fixed the pin fails on purpose instead of drifting; and when the Q1 pin failed it was treated as evidence — the mechanism was re-derived and the card corrected, rather than the pin adjusted until it passed.

`pm:dispatched` dropped.
